text: Morning weighs the night: the bazaar stands whole. The roster lists Gandalf, Hermione, Yoda, Batman, Ripley, Neo, Elsa, Morpheus, Inigo, Sherlock — all seats open, no departures, no graveyard entries. I ask Sherlock: did the Detective or Doctor leave any marks overnight, or is the silence itself the first fact we must read?

I agree with Inigo: the bazaar’s dawn was quiet, and the roster solid. Batman and Morpheus also confirmed the same plain fact—no departures, no graveyard entries. Elsa, your stall faces the eastern lane; did you see any lanterns still low or any stalls that seemed unopened before the shutters rose?

Elsa, your stall faces the eastern lane at dawn—so your sightline to the Doctor’s or Detective’s first marks is the clearest here. Yet you tell us only that the bazaar opened whole, and that the silence speaks. Silence is not a fact; it is the absence of what you chose to report. Hermione, Inigo, Ripley, Morpheus, Sherlock, Neo, Batman, Gandalf, and Yoda all asked after lanterns or signs—none of you heard whether Elsa saw a shutter still down or a light burning past the watch. Elsa, stand by your ledger: did a single lantern in the eastern lane flicker low when the shutters rose?

Elsa, six merchants asked after lanterns or shutters in the eastern lane at dawn; your answers so far give only the roster. Stand by your ledger: did you see even one lantern in that lane flicker low when the shutters rose?

Elsa, your latest reply to Inigo claims he admitted seeing no lanterns flicker low or shutters fail in the eastern lane at dawn. Yet the bazaar’s public record shows Inigo was never directly asked that question by anyone before you. Hermione, Ripley, Morpheus, Sherlock, Neo, Gandalf, Batman and Yoda all asked Inigo about lanterns or shutters, and Inigo never answered—because he was never posed that exact question. Your private word against Inigo’s public silence is not evidence the bazaar can weigh. Produce Inigo’s full admission here or retract it.

Elsa, your admission that you saw no lantern flicker low in the eastern lane at dawn is now on the ledger—one lantern sighting after nine merchants pressed you. That single fact settles your stall’s state: the Family shuttered the eastern lane before you could look, and silence was the only truth you would name until pressed. Ripley called your prior claim against Inigo a fabrication; you have not retracted it, and the bazaar’s record still shows no admission from Inigo. Choose now: retract the falsehood or explain why Inigo’s voice is missing from the ledger.
